newsitem.title: USA: CBOT RICE ENDS LOWER ON LARGE PRODUCTION FORECAST.
newsitem.headline: CBOT RICE ENDS LOWER ON LARGE PRODUCTION FORECAST.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended with modest losses Tuesday in response to a U.S. Department of Agriculture forecast showing a large crop, traders said.
"We've got a big rice crop coming," said one floor trader.
USDA put 1997/98 (Aug/July) rice production at 182 million hundredweight (cwt), which is six percent above the crop in 1996 and five percent above the crop harvested two years ago, USDA said.
Traders said it was likely that the market would trend lower through the harvest period this fall because inventories are high and farmers have plenty of selling left to do.
One trader said his intermediate downside target for September was $9.45 per cwt, followed by $9.20.
Despite projections for lower prices, the market should remain underpinned by robust domestic demand and good U.S. exports, traders said.
In its lastest supply and demand forecast, USDA raised U.S. exports to 82 million cwt from 79 million in July.
Rice ended four to five cents per cwt lower with September down five at $9.62. Volume was estimated by CBOT at 250 lots, compared with Monday's actual volume of 365 lots.
